info.title: Index Solutions API
info.description:
# API for Index Solutions Services

All API endpoints require authorization with a Bearer token in the Authorization header. The token can be retrieved from the OAuth 2.0 token endpoint. More information regarding this endpoint can be found in the [AWS Cognito documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/token-endpoint.html).

## Contact Monitoring
For Contact Monitoring we attempt to find a public profile for the contact and monitor that profile for changes over time. We then notify those who are subscribed to updates about relevant changes to the contact or the underlying public profile.

The input to a Contact Monitoring Request is a contact (with required name and some additional information such as job title/company or email) as well as configuration options.

## Entity Resolution
During an Entity Resolution we attempt to find the most likely ID in the requested database (i.e. either the DUNS number or S&P ID). Depending on the configuration option the result also includes fields like legal name, primary address, Global Ultimate Parent, NAICS Codes, and SALI Codes.

The input to an Entity Resolution Request is a company name and a location (optional but highly recommended for best results) as well as configuration options to control the type of data to be returned.

## Matter Classification
The Matter Classification API allows you to classify a matter into one or more areas of law or services.

## Timecard Classification
The Timecard Classification API allows you to classify individual time entries (timecards) into specific legal services using the SALI (Standards Advancement for the Legal Industry) taxonomy. Timecards are submitted under an existing matter and include a narrative describing the work performed. Our system analyzes the narrative and assigns appropriate SALI service classifications, helping standardize billing and matter management practices.

## Webhooks
Webhooks allow you to receive timely notifications about updates to monitored contacts, entities, or profiles. You can configure webhooks to listen for specific types of events and receive updates when changes occur.

To use webhooks:
1. Create a webhook endpoint on your server to receive POST requests from our system.
2. Register your webhook URL using the create webhook API endpoint.
3. Configure the types of events you want to receive (profile updates, contact updates, entity updates).
4. Our system will send POST requests to your webhook URL whenever relevant events occur.

Webhook payloads include details about the event type and the updated data, allowing you to keep your systems in sync with the latest information from Index Solutions.

Webhooks and events are a single shared surface: any resource read scope you have been granted (`bch.external/contact.read`, `bch.external/organization.read`, `bch.external/matter.read` or `bch.external/timecard.read`) gives access to it, and the events you receive are always scoped to your own project.

### Webhook Signature Verification
Each webhook request includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header containing an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the payload. When you create a webhook, the response includes a `secret` field. Use this secret to verify incoming webhook requests:
``` signature = HMAC-SHA256(JSON.stringify(payload), secret) ```
Compare the computed signature with the `X-Webhook-Signature` header value to ensure the request originated from Index Solutions.

### Event Types

**contact-updated:** We have discovered an update to the underlying contact resource that should be integrated to your system.

**contact-profile-updated:** We have discovered an update to the profile associated with the contact resource. If you track profiles separately, your system should be updated.

**organization-updated:** We have discovered an update to the underlying organization resource that should be integrated to your system.

**matter-updated:** We have classified a matter into one or more areas of law or services. Where a matter's timecards are summarized before classification, this event is also sent when the synthesized outputs (derived description, reasoning, key insights) are produced. Classifications published in this event are confirmed: provisional labels produced by an interim pass are not sent. `change.patch` may be an empty array when the event confirms a state rather than altering it — `matter` always carries the current resource. `matter.rollup` reflects the timecard mix at the time of the event and may lag `GET /matters/{id}` while a matter's timecards are still being classified. The same `(id, changedAt)` idempotency guidance as `timecard-updated` applies.

**timecard-updated:** We have classified a timecard into one or more areas of law or services. An event is sent each time a timecard's classification completes — a timecard that is re-classified after its matter is re-synthesized or re-classified emits again, with new classifications.

Make your handler idempotent on `(payload.timecard.id, payload.change.changedAt)` — equivalently `(payload.change.resource.uri, payload.change.changedAt)` — and treat the highest `changedAt` as authoritative; apply an event only if its `changedAt` is newer than the last one you stored for that timecard. Do not deduplicate on the event `id`: every delivery carries a new one, including legitimate re-classifications. Deliveries may arrive out of order or more than once.

Other timecard writes, including deletion, do not emit an event.

**workflow-failed:** Processing of a resource could not be completed. The payload carries the resource id and the originating change; no resource body is included.

get.summary: Get Organization Profiles for the Global Operating, Financial, and Related Entity Parents of the Organization with a given ID
get.description:
This API endpoint fetches the Profiles for a given Organization ID.  The Global Ultimate is the ultimate "operating" parent. The Global Financial Ultimate is the ultimate "financial" parent and will roll up higher than the Global Ultimate when the parent is a financial entity. The Global Related Entity rolls up the highest and will include affiliates that may not have direct ownership but is useful for clustering.
Corporate hierarchy is separately licensed. Accounts without it receive `403` for every value of `referenceType` — including `parent` — rather than an empty result, so a missing parent is never ambiguous. `404` means the Organization ID itself is unknown.

post.description: Create a new matter with classification configuration. Matter Players are optional but recommended for better results.

requestBody.description: A JSON object containing a matter payload

allOf.description: Legal Matter. Should include a title and description in most cases. typeDescription and department are not available in all systems but should be provided if available.

id.description: ID in external system

description.description: Detailed description of the matter. This is the Narrative Description Text in the SALI Matter Record.
examples: Litigation involving termination of purchase order and claim for damage
Assist client with Vendor Agreements with XYZ Client

derivedDescription.description: System-generated matter description synthesized from the matter's timecard narratives by the directory timecard-synthesis pipeline. Used as background context for downstream timecard classification. Read-only.

synthesisReasoning.description: Reasoning that produced the synthesized derivedDescription. Read-only; absent until the matter's timecards have been synthesized.

keyInsights.description: Key insights derived for the matter during synthesis, one per entry. Read-only; absent until the matter's timecards have been synthesized.

rollup.description: Hours-weighted distribution of the matter's classified timecards by their primary SALI service classification, maintained by the directory timecard-synthesis pipeline. Background signal for downstream classification; absent until the matter's timecards have been classified.

classDistribution.description: Keyed by the timecard's primary service classification value ('generic' for generic entries).

timelineDigest.description: Populated on the internal matter reads and the classification workflow/task payloads only — it is a classification input, not a matter output, and the public External API does not return it. Present on this shared schema because the timecard/matter classify payloads inherit it.

firstActivityDate.description: ISO date of the matter's earliest timecard entry.

lastActivityDate.description: ISO date of the matter's latest timecard entry.

datasetCutoffDate.description: Latest timecard date across the matter's source dataset (file or project). The reference point for recency: a matter whose lastActivityDate trails this date by more than stalledThresholdDays has gone quiet relative to the dataset.

stalledThresholdDays.description: Inactivity window (days, relative to datasetCutoffDate) the deployment treats as a stall signal. Configured per customer; a soft signal for classification, not a hard rule.

months.description: Per-month activity aggregates in chronological order.

earliestNarratives.description: Sample narratives from the start of the matter's timeline, chronological.

latestNarratives.description: Sample narratives from the end of the matter's timeline, chronological. Terminal language here (closing, dismissal, settlement, deal collapse) is the primary completion-event evidence.

items.description: A dated narrative sample from the matter's timecard timeline.

practiceGroup.description: Practice group responsible for the matter — the smaller organizational unit within a department (a department typically spans several practice groups). Firm-internal label; the firm supplies the value set. Provide when available.

matterType.description: Matter type as defined in the Firm's Matter Type Taxonomy

classificationStatus.description: Lifecycle status values for matter classification.

id.description: ID of player in external system

dataSource.description: The data source to use for the matter classification.

value.description: A SALI Service class or subclass value. The value is intentionally not enumerated in the schema: the authoritative value list is the SALI Service taxonomy reference data (e.g. sali/labels/Service.json shipped with the services), which is large and updated independently of this contract. Producers validate emitted values against that taxonomy reference data.

isPrimary.description: Whether the classification is the primary classification for the matter

hierarchy.description: The full hierarchical path from major class to this value

id.description: IRI of the service

value.description: A SALI Area of Law value. The Area of Law provides context to the process — the primary subject of law involved (for example, "He prosecuted the defendant" is criminal law; "She prosecuted the patent" is intellectual property law); a matter may carry multiple areas of law. The value is intentionally not enumerated in the schema: the authoritative value list is the SALI Area of Law taxonomy reference data (e.g. sali/labels/Area of Law.json shipped with the services), which is large and updated independently of this contract. id.description: IRI of the area of law

id.description: IRI of the area of law

anyOf.description: A classification from a customer-specific label taxonomy, applied to a matter or timecard after the baseline SALI classification. The taxonomy defines the label set and which subject (matter or timecard) it applies to.

taxonomyId.description: The id of a label taxonomy for matter/timecard classification. An unconstrained string: validity of a given taxonomyId is owned by the tasks service at classification-creation time, not by this schema. Index-derived custom-label taxonomies follow the naming convention `ServiceOffering1`, `ServiceOfferingType1`, `MatterStage1`, `MatterStatus1`, `ClientMatterRole1`, `Activity1`, `Task1`; client-provided (firm) rows follow the `Activity2` / `Task2` convention. These ids are anonymous on purpose so they can't be used to identify our customers, since they might be exposed in a public API in the future.

value.description: The label name from the custom taxonomy

id.description: The label code within the custom taxonomy

confidence.description: Model confidence for this label, reported per label to support per-field acceptance evaluation

isPrimary.description: Whether the classification is the primary label within its taxonomy

anyOf.description: A classification supplied by the client firm (client-provided provenance), applied to a matter or timecard alongside Index-derived classifications. Structurally identical to CustomClassification but with `source` const `firm`: the label vocabulary is open (no reference-taxonomy resolution) and validity of the `taxonomyId`/`value` is owned by the producing service at creation time, not by this schema.

id.description: The client-provided label code (open vocabulary)

confidence.description: Model confidence for this label, reported per label to support per-field acceptance evaluation

isPrimary.description: Whether the classification is the primary label within its taxonomy

allOf.description: Shared base for product configurations that supports an optional retention window.

ttl.description: Optional retention window in days. Must be one of 7, 30, or 90. When set, the object and its co-located secondary records (e.g. changesets; a matter's timecards) are removed via DynamoDB TTL at least this many days after the most recent create/upsert. Latest request wins: re-POSTing with a ttl resets the expiry window, and re-POSTing without a ttl (omitted or null) clears any previously set expiry, meaning no TTL. Deletion timing is approximate — after expiry, deletion typically occurs within minutes to ~48h.
